![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14095879/assets/47a2bf6e4f16a4a62636c0d7cdcda38fa6d6aecdcc4081dc8671549aab2b36fd.png)

Consider the triangle $Δ$ in the $uv$-plane, given by

$$
Δ={(u,v)\,:\,0\le u\le 2,\,1\le v\le \frac{1}{2}u+1}.
$$

The transformation $T$ is defined as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Which of the following gives the image of $Δ$ in the $xy$-plane under the action of $T?$
worked_solution:
An affine transformation $T:{R}^{2}\to {R}^{2}$ is a function of the form

$$
x=Au+b,
$$

where $x,u,$ and $b$ are column vectors in ${R}^{2},$ and $A$ is a $2\times 2$ matrix.

Notice that the given transformation is already in matrix form 

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}] & ={{[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{A}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{u}+{{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{b}\end{aligned}
$$

The transformation $T$ maps the boundary of $Δ$ to the boundary of the image. So, to find the image of $Δ,$ we find the images of each side.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14095879/assets/5c38b3ccfc99ca173324e4caf4585e07991162c75741b20b5d288ce73ad0ff98.png)

             

To quickly carry out this calculation, we set up the following matrices:

- The matrix $U$ containing all vertices of our triangle:

$$
U=[\begin{aligned}0 & 2 & 2 \\ 1 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}]
$$

- The matrix $B$ that has the same shape as $U$ and with the vector $b$ in each column:

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

The image of $u$ under $T$ is given by $Au+b.$ So, by applying $T$ to $U,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}AU+B & =[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 & 2 & 2 \\ 1 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & -1 & -2 \\ 0 & 2 & 2\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & -1 \\ 1 & 3 & 3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the vertices of the image in the $xy$-plane are $(0,1),(0,3),$ and $(-1,3).$

Drawing this region in the $xy$-plane, we get the following:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14095879/assets/1bcadc0b9909159ebf99280e8d47d52891d2aa8653d9bc89bb2a3bb8363d4fb1.png)

          

Finally, since $det(A)=1>0,$ this transformation preserves orientation.
